title: 2.8 Equipment Protection
description: ESD protection, power fluctuations and power protection devices

questions.question: What does ESD stand for?
What is ESD (Electrostatic Discharge)?
options: A method of storing data on a hard drive
A sudden flow of electricity between two objects caused by a static charge imbalance
A type of wired network connection
A gradual increase in a computer's processing speed
questions.correctAnswer: A sudden flow of electricity between two objects caused by a static charge imbalance

questions.question: Why is ESD a concern when handling computer equipment?
options: It increases the storage capacity of hard drives
It can damage sensitive electronic components
It strengthens the connection of network cables
It improves the performance of circuit boards
questions.correctAnswer: It can damage sensitive electronic components

questions.question: Which ESD protection measure ensures that equipment and personnel are properly grounded to prevent static buildup?
What should be used when handling sensitive electronic components to dissipate static charges?
What is the purpose of ESD bags and containers?
options: To increase the voltage supplied to the equipment
To cool the components during operation
To store and transport sensitive equipment/components by shielding them from static charges
To provide backup power during outages
questions.correctAnswer: To store and transport sensitive equipment/components by shielding them from static charges

questions.question: A short-term drop in voltage, typically caused by sudden increases in power demand or faults in the power distribution system, is called what?
A brief increase in voltage, often caused by lightning strikes or switching operations, is called what?
A rapid increase in voltage that lasts for a short duration, usually caused by switching off high-powered devices or sudden load changes, is called what?
A complete loss of power supply for a brief period due to faults, outages or tripped circuit breakers is called what?
What term describes sudden, brief fluctuations in voltage caused by electrical disturbances such as lightning, EMI or switching operations?
Which power protection device absorbs excess voltage spikes and redirects them away from connected equipment?
Which device gives battery backup and provides power during a power outage?
What does UPS stand for?
Which features do UPS systems typically include?
options: Wired networking, audio output and video output
Recycling programs, data wiping and donation options
Surge protection, battery backup and voltage regulation
questions.correctAnswer: Surge protection, battery backup and voltage regulation

questions.question: Which device stabilizes incoming voltage to ensure a steady supply to connected equipment, compensating for voltage sags and surges?
Which device isolates equipment from the main power supply and protects against voltage spikes and transient noise?
Which device regulates voltage, filters out noise and provides surge protection to ensure clean and stable power?
What does the device called an AVR do?
options: It provides battery backup during a power outage
It monitors voltage levels and automatically adjusts them to maintain a stable output voltage within a specified range
It removes noise and interference from audio devices
questions.correctAnswer: It monitors voltage levels and automatically adjusts them to maintain a stable output voltage within a specified range

questions.question: What does AVR stand for?
Which device removes noise and interference from the power supply to protect sensitive equipment from electrical disturbances?
True or False: ESD mats on work surfaces and ESD flooring help protect static-sensitive equipment.
True or False: UPS systems provide battery backup and protect against voltage sags, surges and interruptions.
